title: Pentecost
hookLine: pray for the gifts every year
tomorrow: does God take the summer off when you do?

cards: Some people want a sign they can feel: goosebumps at the bridge of a song, a voice, a certainty you can't argue with. Acts gives Pentecost signs like that.

A sound from heaven like a mighty wind, tongues like fire resting on each of them, and the disciples speaking so that visitors from many nations hear them in their own languages. A Catholic is confirmed once.
So why does the Church pray every Pentecost, come, Holy Spirit, as if for the first time?

teach.b: Two real answers live inside the Church. One view looks first to the quiet gifts.

teach.h: BEST CASE: THE SPIRIT WORKS UNSEEN.
teach.b: Isaiah names them resting on the coming king, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, the spirit of counsel, and of fortitude, the spirit of knowledge, and of godliness," and then, "he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord."

Seven. The catechism calls these gifts lasting dispositions that make a person ready to follow the Spirit's lead. Its best case: the Spirit can work unseen, and chasing a feeling can make you miss what is quietly growing.
You grow into the gifts like a muscle you didn't know you had.
The other view, alive in the Catholic charismatic renewal, also prays openly for the gifts Paul lists: healing, prophecy, tongues, expected now, not only then.

teach.h: BEST CASE: ASK BOLDLY, LIKE ACTS.
teach.b: Its best case: Acts isn't just history. The same Spirit comes again, and asking boldly is how the first disciples prayed.
Paul holds both in one sentence: "Now there are diversities of graces, but the same Spirit."
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: confirmation is never repeated, yet every Pentecost Mass asks again, come, Holy Spirit. Once given, and asked for every year.

how: At Pentecost, Catholics wear red at Mass and sing the sequence Veni, Sancte Spiritus (Come, Holy Spirit); some pray a novena to the Holy Spirit in the nine days before.

o: the feast of Jesus's baptism in the river
the day Jesus was taken up to heaven
the fiftieth-day feast when the Spirit came

games.q: the Spirit's gifts — tap the pairs.

s: Catholics are confirmed again every Pentecost
confirmation is given once. Pentecost prays for the Spirit to come again.
Isaiah's list ends with the fear of the Lord
he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord.
the Spirit's gifts always come with a feeling you can't miss
the catechism calls them lasting dispositions; they can work quietly.

games.q: you lean toward the quiet gifts. your friend at youth group prays boldly for healing and tongues. what is her view's best case?
o: the same Spirit still comes, and asking boldly is how Acts prays.
a strong feeling is the only real proof the Spirit is there.
the seven quiet gifts were only meant for the first apostles.
games.why: that's the charismatic view at its best. Paul holds both: diversities of graces, but the same Spirit.

practice: Sit with your hands open on your knees, palms up. Choose one gift from Isaiah's list you'd want this year: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, godliness or fear of the Lord.
Hold that one word in your open hands for the sit. If you pray, you can ask for it in your own plain words.

wordCard.voice: Pentecost. The fiftieth day, when the Spirit came, and the feast that asks for the Spirit again each year.

orig.note: Latin: come, Holy Spirit; the opening of the Pentecost sequence.

carryVoice: Your line: come again. One Spirit, many gifts, asked for again every single year. Until tomorrow.
